# Pose-free and Feed-forward Training

Also called: Feed-forward 3DGS, Generalizable Gaussian Splatting

## Overview
This family reconstructs 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes from uncalibrated or sparse image collections without relying on external Structure-from-Motion pipelines [6136-instantsplat.md, 6137-anysplat.md, 6464-pixelsplat.md, 6888-joint-pose-optimization.md]. It sets itself apart from traditional 3DGS by eliminating iterative pose estimation, and from feed-forward alternatives by either initializing Gaussians via foundation model priors [6136-instantsplat.md] or jointly optimizing poses as learnable parameters [6888-joint-pose-optimization.md].

## Shared principles
Builds on [Learning and Training Methods](9068-learning-and-training-methods.md).

## Subtopics

### [InstantSplat](6136-instantsplat.md)
InstantSplat is a pose-free, sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting method that eliminates the need for Structure-from-Motion pipelines by leveraging geometry priors from foundation models like MASt3R or VGGT [6136-instantsplat.md]. It enables training in seconds by directly initializing Gaussians from these priors, distinguishing itself from feed-forward methods which regress primitives directly from images, and from traditional 3DGS which requires dense pose estimation [6136-instantsplat.md]. Choose this method when rapid reconstruction from very sparse views (3–10 images) is required without iterative optimization.

### [AnySplat](6137-anysplat.md)
AnySplat is a pose-free feed-forward network that reconstructs 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes from uncalibrated image collections without requiring camera pose annotations [6137-anysplat.md]. It predicts 3D Gaussian primitives and per-image intrinsics and extrinsics in a single forward pass [6137-anysplat.md]. Unlike sibling methods, it scales to casual dense or sparse multi-view captures, matches pose-aware baselines, and surpasses prior pose-free methods in zero-shot evaluations at real-time rendering latency [6137-anysplat.md]. Choose this method when handling arbitrary multi-view captures where pose data is unavailable and real-time inference is needed.

### [pixelSplat](6464-pixelsplat.md)
pixelSplat is a feed-forward model that reconstructs a 3D radiance field parameterized by 3D Gaussian primitives from a pair of input images, enabling real-time and memory-efficient rendering [6464-pixelsplat.md]. It solves the problem of local minima inherent to sparse, locally supported representations in generalizable novel view synthesis, where non-differentiable pruning or splitting cannot be applied because gradients must back-propagate through the representation [6464-pixelsplat.md]. Unlike light-field transformers which produce black-box ray colors, pixelSplat generates an explicit, editable 3D representation [6464-pixelsplat.md]. Choose this method when working with stereo pairs and requiring an explicit, editable 3D representation with real-time rendering.

### [Joint Pose Optimization](6888-joint-pose-optimization.md)
Joint Pose Optimization refers to methods that simultaneously optimize camera poses and the scene representation to eliminate the dependency on pre-computed Structure-from-Motion pipelines [6888-joint-pose-optimization.md]. This approach relaxes the strict requirement for known camera parameters, allowing novel-view synthesis from unposed images using only photometric loss [6888-joint-pose-optimization.md]. It distinguishes itself from pose-free feed-forward methods by iteratively refining poses during training rather than predicting them in a single forward pass, though it typically requires rough initialization and is limited to small motions [6888-joint-pose-optimization.md]. Choose this method when iterative refinement is acceptable and camera motions are relatively small, avoiding the need for a trained feed-forward network.

### [Loss Scheduling for Candidate Head](13095-loss-scheduling-for-candidate-head.md)
Loss scheduling for the candidate head is a training strategy that gradually reduces the influence of an image-dependent 'candidate head' ($\hat{C}_i$) during optimization, transitioning to a shared representation ($\hat{C}$) to stabilize pose estimation for hard-pose images [13095-loss-scheduling-for-candidate-head.md]. It prevents the shared representation from being distracted by wrong supervision introduced by hard-pose images in the early stages, allowing the model to assimilate these images into the shared representation once the shared model is accurate enough [13095-loss-scheduling-for-candidate-head.md]. This method is distinct from sibling methods by explicitly decoupling the training influence of per-image heads via a cosine schedule rather than relying solely on joint pose optimization or fixed head structures [13095-loss-scheduling-for-candidate-head.md]. Choose this method when training models with per-image candidate heads to stabilize pose estimation for challenging or hard-pose images.

### VS-Splat Extension for Noisy Camera Poses
An extension to handle noisy camera poses, following the SHARE implementation with a modified input module [S1, unofficial]. It uses three 1×1 2D convolutional layers to reduce the channel dimension of feature maps from 768 to 128, matching the SHARE input dimension, with each convolutional layer preceded by a normalization layer and a Swish activation [S1, unofficial]. Due to GPU memory constraints, the number of fine-grained primitives per voxel $M$ is set to 8 [S1, unofficial]. On the CO3D dataset, this extension yields a PSNR of 21.62, SSIM of 0.864, and LPIPS of 0.211 [S1, unofficial]. Choose this variant when the input camera poses are noisy and require robust feature alignment similar to SHARE.

## Background
The family originates from the need to generalize 3D Gaussian Splatting beyond single-scene optimization, which is computationally expensive and requires accurate initial poses [6464-pixelsplat.md]. Early work like [pixelSplat](6464-pixelsplat.md) introduced feed-forward architectures to predict Gaussian primitives directly from image pairs, addressing the local minima issues of traditional splatting [6464-pixelsplat.md]. Subsequent developments like [InstantSplat](6136-instantsplat.md) and [AnySplat](6137-anysplat.md) incorporated foundation model priors to enable pose-free reconstruction from sparse or uncalibrated views, significantly reducing training time to seconds [6136-instantsplat.md, 6137-anysplat.md]. [Joint Pose Optimization](6888-joint-pose-optimization.md) provides an alternative by treating poses as learnable parameters rather than predicting them via a network [6888-joint-pose-optimization.md]. These methods are used in generalizable novel view synthesis, 3D object reconstruction from sparse views, and applications requiring real-time rendering from casual captures [6464-pixelsplat.md, S1, unofficial].
